::: {.eyebrow}
A guided route through bioacoustics
:::

This page will collect resources that are genuinely useful for learning and doing bioacoustics. Instead of becoming a long unannotated link list, each recommendation will explain what it teaches, what background it assumes, and when it becomes useful in a real project.

::: {.feature-grid}
::: {.feature-card}
### Video tutorials

Approachable demonstrations of recording, annotation, acoustic measurement, visualization, and analysis.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### Software and packages

Useful tools in R, Python, and specialist bioacoustics software, grouped by the problem they solve.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### Methods papers

Recommended papers with a short note on the central idea, practical value, assumptions, and limitations.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### Field-to-analysis workflows

Practical pathways from recorder setup and metadata to quality checks, reproducible analysis, and archiving.
:::
:::

## Planned learning paths

1. **Starting with sound** — recordings, spectrograms, annotation, and acoustic features.
2. **Working reproducibly** — project organization, metadata, code, and version control.
3. **Studying sequences** — units, transitions, alignment, and higher-order structure.
4. **Connecting sound and social life** — behavioural data, interaction, and social networks.
